title: Radio broadcasts and Eddie Randall's help in 1935
summary: They almost starve the first summer until Eddie Randall, whose band Miles Davis later joined, books them in small Illinois towns.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: And, we used to broadcast every Wednesday night, amateur night,
Yeah. Oh, yes, we almost starved to death the first summer we were here. There's a bandleader here

named Eddie Randall, Eddie Randall is -- is -- is the bandleader that Miles Davis -- the first band that Miles Davis played with was Eddie Randall's band. Eddie Randall's the type of fella that he's been very kind to musicians. He was very broadminded, a big person. And Eddie had a small band and he had bought a seven-passenger Chrysler and he was popular in all the little small towns out here.

All southern Illinois. And he worked every week, and so he took us up to O'Fallon, Illinois, it's a little coal mining town and we -- he had the people promote us up there at a big dance. We took the band up there and we made around $14.00-$15.00 a piece. And that money sure came in handy, because we suffered hard, because we were new here in St. Louis, and we just didn't know our way around and Eddie did all he -- Eddie Randall did all he could to help him. I shall never forget that. That was the summer of 1935.
